Police are investigating the incident and seeking cost recovery for the damaged equipment.

title: BCI-NALSAR row: Who is Manan Kumar Mishra and why is he in spotlight?
content: Bar Council of India chairman Manan Kumar Mishra is central to a recent controversy.  The council's directive against NALSAR graduates was withdrawn after widespread criticism.  Students have a right to protest, the Supreme Court observed on Friday.  The BCI's role in this matter was questioned by the apex court.  Proceedings were closed after considering various representations from the public.

title: Manav Suthar: The all-weather finger spinner India needs after Ravindra Jadeja
content: Manav Suthar is a classical left-arm spinner who stands out in modern cricket for his artistry, skill, and dedication. Praised by experts like Maninder Singh, Suthar impresses with his seamless action, wrist magic, and high revolutions on the ball. His adaptability and work ethic have earned him recognition in both domestic and international cricket, marking him as replacement for Ravindra Jadeja and an all-weather finger spinner.

title: US lost 45 Reaper drones in Iran war, representing 25% fleet worth $1.3 bn: Report
content: The US military has faced the loss of forty-five MQ-9 Reaper drones amid its ongoing tensions with Iran. This figure not only highlights a considerable depletion of their fleet but also signifies a financial hit exceeding one billion dollars. The drones have been heavily deployed around the Strait of Hormuz, revealing their susceptibility.

title: Oracle layoffs: Managers asked to pick employees to 'fire' before September 1
content: Oracle is planning fresh layoffs this month, with managers reportedly asked to identify employees whose roles will go before its second fiscal quarter opens on September 1. Some teams face double-digit percentage cuts. The move follows a year in which Oracle eliminated 21,000 jobs, spent $1.8 billion on restructuring, and poured $55.7 billion into AI data centres.

title: 'Astronauts' land on road craters: Over 100 Jaipur residents stage unique protest

Two individuals dressed as astronauts entered water-filled potholes, simulating a lunar landscape. This unusual demonstration aimed to draw attention to neglected infrastructure and drainage issues. Residents have sought attention from local officials for several months regarding these problems. Tenders for road and drainage work have been awarded and will commence after the monsoon.

title: Robot found 4,500-year-old sealed Great Pyramid door: Here's what happened
content: A robot has ventured into a concealed corridor within the Great Pyramid of Giza, uncovering a sealed barrier potentially dating back 4,500 years. This intriguing find reopens inquiries regarding the secrets held by this ancient structure. Employing contemporary technology, researchers were able to investigate sections previously unreachable by humans. Continued exploration may unveil significant insights into the original architecture of the pyramid.

title: Mitchell Starc surpasses Kapil Dev as Australia face Bangladesh nightmare
content: In a remarkable achievement, Mitchell Starc outstripped Kapil Dev's wicket tally during the opening Test against Bangladesh, now boasting 435 Test wickets, positioning him eleventh on the all-time list. Meanwhile, Tanzid Hasan Tamim made history by scoring his first Test century in Australia. As the second day concluded, Bangladesh enjoyed a 150-run advantage, placing Australia in a tough spot to stay competitive in the series.

title: Colorado expands habitat protection for endangered Preble's jumping mouse
content: Colorado is taking significant steps to ensure the survival of the endangered Preble's meadow jumping mouse. Efforts focus on restoring essential streamside ecosystems and linking them to floodplains. Landowners are invited to join this initiative through voluntary conservation measures and financial support. A conservation bank was established in 2024 to facilitate these vital restoration projects, with new initiatives rolling out in 2026 to enhance habitat safeguarding.

title: Sam Altman says he is happy he rejected Goldman Sachs job offer
content: Sam Altman, OpenAI CEO, shared his college decision to reject a Goldman Sachs internship. He found the corporate path hierarchical and less appealing than building startups.  Altman believes artificial intelligence now lowers barriers for students to launch companies independently.  This technology empowers young entrepreneurs to create products and make progress easily.  Therefore, rejecting prestigious opportunities is becoming a simpler choice for students today.

title: South Korea unveils housing package to boost supply and support young buyers
content: In a bid to boost housing options and assist first-time buyers, South Korea has unveiled new initiatives aimed at young home seekers. The government plans to provide enhanced support for construction financing, allowing for market stabilization. Furthermore, fresh lending facilities will be available for youth and newlywed couples looking to secure their dream homes.

title: Trust paid £3,000 to save Shakespeare's birthplace from being shipped to US
content: In the 1840s, Shakespeare's birthplace in Stratford-upon-Avon faced the threat of sale, as American showman P.T. Barnum aimed to move the historic home to New York. A dedicated committee formed, rallying public donations and support from notable figures like Prince Albert to save the site. Their efforts culminated in the successful acquisition of the house at auction in 1847, ensuring the preservation of this cherished cultural landmark.

title: Indian-origin man rejected for H-1B 3 times finds another way to stay in US
content: Sohan Sethi faced multiple H-1B visa rejections after arriving in the United States. He then pursued an O-1 visa, requiring extensive documentation and lawyer fees. Sethi demonstrated extraordinary ability through achievements and industry recognition to secure his stay. This path highlights the challenges faced by skilled professionals seeking to remain in America. He now manages a team, sharing his experience to guide others through the process.

title: Iran prez to visit India for BRICS summit amid Middle East tensions
content: Iran has signalled that it sees India as a potential partner in efforts to ease tensions in West Asia, with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying New Delhi could play a greater role in de-escalating the ongoing crisis. Araghchi made the remarks during his visit to India in June. He said Tehran did not see a military solution to the conflict and believed that negotiations offered only viable way forward.

Players require time to adapt to different conditions and formats of play. Team India begins its campaign against Sri Lanka in Galle, a venue known for spin. He also kicked her after people intervened in the incident. The police are currently searching for the accused shopkeeper. Efforts are underway to locate the missing woman beggar and her child.

title: TATA Steel sells 100% stake in Jamshedpur FC to Churchill Brothers

The agreement includes the transfer of the ISL sporting rights to Churchill Brothers Sports Club, as well as the contracts for players and coaching staff, which will move to the Goa-based club starting September 2026. This strategic decision allows Tata Steel to focus on enhancing grassroots football initiatives.

title: NALSAR row explained: Students' protest over CJI's invite, BCI's flip-flop, SC steps in
content: The Bar Council of India encountered significant backlash for its initial directive affecting NALSAR law students. Following public outcry and intervention from the Supreme Court, the Council revoked its order. The Supreme Court upheld the students' rights to engage in protest and converse with the Chief Justice. As a result, the Bar Council has retracted its earlier circular, and the matter is now subject to further Supreme Court review.

title: PMAY-U 2.0 in Kerala: Who gets Rs 4 lakh housing assistance and how it is funded

The Centre will provide Rs 1.50 lakh, and the state government Rs 1 lakh per house. Municipalities and beneficiaries will contribute the remaining Rs 1.50 lakh for each home. This move ensures Kerala secures Rs 450 crore in central government assistance.

title: Tenant not paying rent? Know how to claim tax relief on unrealised rent
content: In India, landlords are permitted to deduct unpaid rent from their taxable income as unrealised rent, provided they meet certain criteria outlined by the Income Tax Rules. It is important for landlords to select the appropriate Income Tax Return form to ensure they can claim this deduction. Additionally, they must keep relevant documents handy to support their claims.

The White House warns of intensified detection and penalties for such trade practices.  India is categorized in the top-risk tier alongside major industrial economies.  This development complicates ongoing trade negotiations between Washington and New Delhi.

title: 9-month delivery delay, repeated defects: JLR told to replace Rs 1.57 crore luxury SUV

The commission ordered a replacement vehicle or a refund of Rs 1.57 crore. The dealer also faced liability for significant delivery delays and missing accessories. Compensation was awarded for mental agony and litigation costs.

title: Fatal US Apache crash puts spotlight back on killer helicopter's safety record
content: The Apache helicopter boasts a strong combat history and advanced capabilities.  However, its operational philosophy contributes to a significant number of recent crashes.  Since 1980, the aircraft has been involved in numerous incidents, resulting in aircraft loss.  The US Army reports a higher mishap rate for Apaches compared to other helicopters.  Recent accidents highlight concerns regarding the helicopter's safety record.

title: Pakistan joins China Moon race with Jinnah-1 rover; mission in 2029

Jinnah-1 will conduct scientific research on plasma, radiation, and lunar geology. This collaboration marks a significant milestone for Pakistan's space program. The mission aims to explore the lunar south pole's potential resources and human activity.

title: Fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya extradited from UAE
content: India's Narcotics Control Bureau has secured the extradition of Virender Singh Basoya from the UAE. Basoya is accused of orchestrating a multi-crore cocaine syndicate and fled the country. This significant development follows sustained inter-agency coordination and international legal action. The Union Home Minister confirmed the successful apprehension of the fugitive drug trafficker. Investigators will now interrogate Basoya regarding the drug cartel's operations and accomplices.

NEW DELHI: Union health minister JP Nadda was admitted to AIIMS Delhi on Thursday evening after experiencing uneasiness, the hospital said. Nadda was evaluated and underwent tests, including a coronary angiography. He is currently stable and has been admitted to the Department of Cardiology for observation, AIIMS said.

End of Article

title: 'Our red line': Shehbaz Sharif threatens India with 'direct response' over Indus Water Treaty
content: shehbaz Sharif threatens a 'direct response' to new Delhi's move . he said the move came days after the Pahalgam terror attack in jammu and Kashmir . new Delhi has proved itsel to keep the IWT in abeyance following the attack .

title: ‘Not scared’: Sukhbir Singh Badal after discharge from hospital day after attack in Nanded
content: sukhbir Singh Badal was discharged from hospital on friday . the former deputy chief minister emerged from the hospital with his arm in a sling . he said he was “not afraid” in his first reaction to the attack . Badal also sought to draw a link between the earlier attack on him at amritsar’s Golden Temple in December 2024 .

title: 'Uncalled for': CJI pulls up Bar Council of India over threat of action against NALSAR students
content: a section of students objected to the university inviting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at its convocation ceremony . the enrolment of 2026 graduates of Hyderabad's NALSAR university of law was revoked by the bar Council of India .

title: Savarkar defamation case: SC quashes Lucknow Court order summoning Rahul
content: the defamation case stems from Rahul Gandhi’s remarks about VD Savarkar . the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha had challenged td savarkar in 2022 . a bench of the high court held that the required sanction had not been obtained .

title: Phuket-Delhi A320 which plunged 300 feet lost flight controls for 4 seconds: Probe
content: airbus says the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured . the aircraft's autopilot was disconnected and the aircraft’s nose went up (increase in pitch) all timings are in IST .

title: Delhi HC, IGI airport, 3 govt offices get bomb threats ahead of Independence Day
content: the threats were reported to the Fire Control Room . the threatening email reportedly referred to August 15 and carried the warning, “Lal Qila ta nishana hove ga” (the Red Fort will be targeted) it also claimed that those carrying out the bombing would be dressed in khaki .

title: New York aquarium study suggests beluga whales may recognise themselves
content: four female beluga whales, three adults named Kathy, Marina and Natasha, were exposed to a large two-way plexiglass mirror and a transparent control surface . the researchers recorded and analysed their behavioural responses across 98 mirror sessions .

title: 'Serious doubts on intent': Congress attacks Centre over caste census format
content: the Congress questioned the Centre's approach to caste enumeration in the upcoming census . the party also alleged that political parties had not been consulted on the questionnaire . it was widely expected that the caste question would include a state-wise list .

title: On cam: Eggs, muck thrown at ex-TMC MLA held in RG Kar victim's 'hurried' cremation case
content: former TMC MLA arrested in connection with alleged 'hurried cremation' of RG K ar victim . he was being escorted to a prison van to be produced before the barrackpore sub-divisional court when the crowd broke through the security cordon .
